---
title: "Study 01 — Bias × size"
subtitle: "Gas-phase (H₂O)₁–₄ · GFN2 · 20 ps · kpush = 0.008 / 0.02 / 0.05"
---

## The bias breaks the weakest bond

Sweeping bias strength `kpush` against cluster size shows the RMSD bias
preferentially rips whatever bond is weakest. A lone water resists and only
**dissociates** at high bias — it has to break a covalent O–H (~5 eV).
Hydrogen-bonded clusters come apart even at the **lowest** bias, because the
intermolecular H-bond (~0.2 eV) snaps first. The tetramer is the most robust,
held by more H-bonds.

![Fraction of the 20 ps run each cluster stayed intact (one fragment, all O–H
present). Reading across a row, more bias breaks clusters sooner.](assets/intact_heatmap.png){width=560}

::: {.callout-tip}
## Takeaway
What breaks depends on what holds the system together: a global-RMSD bias just
maximizes structural novelty, and the cheapest way to do that is to snap the
weakest bond — which for clusters means evaporation, not rearrangement.
:::
